scope: Early non-contrast CT signs of middle-cerebral-artery infarction, and acute CT pulmonary angiography findings of pulmonary embolism.

keyRecommendations.text: Non-contrast CT is the primary imaging test for clinical acute stroke, and early MCA-infarct signs include a hyperdense MCA, loss of the insular ribbon and grey-white junction, and sulcal effacement.
On CT angiography, pulmonary embolism is an intraluminal filling defect that may block the lumen completely or partly, in a central or eccentric position.
CTPA signs of right-ventricular dysfunction include an RV cavity wider than the LV on the short axis (RV/LV ratio greater than 0.9), with or without hepatic-vein reflux and leftward septal shift.

clinicalBottomLine: Read the non-contrast head CT for the named early MCA-infarct signs, remembering that the scan can look normal in nearly 30% of hyperacute infarcts. On CTPA, call PE from an intraluminal filling defect and look for RV dilatation greater than the LV.
notableCaveats: Intracranial haemorrhage signs are not described in the accepted CT-head paper. Railway-track and polo-mint wording in the PE review sits in its MRI paragraph and is not used as a CTPA fact.
